public_rationale: The checkable part is the statement that at most 5GW of data center capacity appeared to be under construction when the post went up. Independent measures from H1 2026 show more. Jefferies (June 2026) counted about 12GW under construction for US capacity due in 2026 alone. CBRE counted 7,481 MW under construction in just eight primary North American markets in H1 2026. BNEF had already counted 23.1GW under construction globally in late 2025. The 5GW figure appears to come from a Sightline/Currence outlook. That figure covered only large projects slated to finish in 2026, not all capacity under construction. Because he set the 5GW against the 30GW to be built by end-2028, the plain reading is total capacity under construction, and that reading is contradicted. The $1 trillion and 30GW requirements are his own modelling and are not scored.
limitations: The result depends on reading '5GW' as total capacity under construction. Under the narrow reading (only capacity scheduled for 2026, large projects), the Currence tracker gives about 5GW, though Jefferies gives 12GW for the US on that same basis.
Trackers differ in scope and definitions.
The revenue and 30GW parts of the sentence were not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: For NVIDIA to keep this going, a trillion dollars in annual revenue is needed by the end of 2028, which would require over 30GW of data center capacity built by then, while only 5GW at most appears to be under construction.
conditions: for NVIDIA to keep this going

statement.excerpt: A trillion dollars in annual revenue is necessary by the end of 2028, which would require over 30GW of data center capacity to be built by then at a time when only 5GW at most appears to be under construction.

from_speaker: A trillion dollars in annual revenue is necessary by the end of 2028
would require over 30GW of data center capacity to be built by then
at a time when only 5GW at most appears to be under construction
our_interpretation: The checkable core is the factual statement about the present: that at most about 5GW of data center capacity appeared to be under construction around the post date (2026-05-26).

The parts saying $1 trillion is 'necessary' and that it 'would require over 30GW' are his own model of what NVIDIA needs. They are a requirement and an inference, not facts that can be observed, so they are not scored here.

Plain reading: because he compares the 5GW with the 30GW that must be built 'by the end of 2028', '5GW under construction' means the total capacity under construction at the time. It does not mean only the subset scheduled to finish in 2026. At a minimum this covers the US, where most of the AI buildout is.
Target period: the first half of 2026. The post says 'at a time when', so the claim describes conditions at publication. H1 2026 is the latest window that public trackers reported on.
If independent trackers show clearly more than 5GW under construction in that window, even in a subset such as US-only or primary markets only, the ceiling of '5GW at most' is contradicted.
criteria.support_condition: Credible trackers or analysts measuring capacity under construction in H1 2026 report about 5GW or less in total, with no credible measure showing materially more.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible trackers or analysts measuring capacity under construction in H1 2026 report materially more than 5GW, even within a subset such as US-only or eight primary markets.

evidence.excerpt: only 12 GW out of 24 GW of datacenter capacity scheduled for 2026 is currently under construction.
evidence.publisher: The Register (reporting a Jefferies research note)
evidence.explanation: Jefferies counted about 12GW under construction in mid-2026 for 2026-scheduled US capacity alone. That is more than twice the '5GW at most' ceiling, even before adding projects due in 2027–28 that had started.

evidence.excerpt: The 7,481 megawatts (MW) under construction in H1 2026 surpassed the previous high reached in 2024.
evidence.explanation: Eight primary North American markets alone had about 7.5GW under construction in H1 2026. These markets exclude many large AI campuses elsewhere, so the total is higher still, and well above 5GW.

evidence.excerpt: As much as 23.1GW of capacity is under construction globally, split across 831 sites.
evidence.explanation: BNEF measured over 23GW of data center IT capacity under construction globally in late 2025. That is before the target period, but it shows the total under construction was far above 5GW shortly before the post.

evidence.excerpt: At least 16GW of capacity is slated to come online in 2026 across roughly 140 projects. Yet only about 5GW is currently under construction.
evidence.locator: quoted excerpt from Sightline/Currence 'Data Center Outlook'
evidence.publisher: Stefano Quintarelli blog (quoting Sightline/Currence Data Center Outlook)
evidence.explanation: This is the likely origin of the 5GW figure. It refers to the subset of large (>50MW) projects slated to come online in 2026, not all capacity under construction. It supports a narrow reading of the claim but not the plain one.
